item.title: GUILTY: Driver banned and fined after illegal taxi operation uncovered at Henley Regatta
item.description: A 67-year-old driver has been banned from driving and fined after being caught offering illegal taxi services during Henley Regatta, one of the busiest events in South Oxfordshire’s calendar. The case was heard at Oxford Magistrates’ Court on Friday 12 December, following an investigation by South Oxfordshire District Council licensing officers. item.title: Liverpool taxi driver reported over tariff breach during tunnel enforcement operation
item.description: Image credit: LCC Licensing A Liverpool licensed taxi driver has been reported for using an incorrect tariff following a joint enforcement operation at the Kingsway Tunnel carried out by Liverpool City Council licensing officers and Mersey Tunnels Police. item.title: Man banned from driving for three years after drink-driving offence in Rotherham
item.description: Image credit: South Yorkshire Police A Rotherham man has been disqualified from driving for three years after appearing before magistrates for a drink-driving offence committed earlier this winter. item.title: Christmas getaway set to be busiest on record as RAC forecasts 37.5m car journeys
item.description: The RAC is forecasting the busiest festive getaway on record, with an estimated 37.5 million car journeys planned in the week leading up to Christmas Day as households across the UK travel to see friends and family. The breakdown and recovery provider said this year’s figure is the highest since it began tracking festive travel patterns in 2013, representing an increase of around eight million trips compared with the 29.3 million estimated last year. item.title: Bolt and Single Homeless Project raise £100,000 through winter ride initiative
item.description: Image credit: Bolt Bolt has raised £100,000 for the Single Homeless Project after running a week-long winter fundraising campaign across its London ride-hailing network, targeting support for people facing homelessness during the coldest part of the year. item.title: Hillingdon Council secures conviction against TfL taxi driver over PSPO breach near Heathrow
item.description: Hillingdon Council has successfully prosecuted a Transport for London licensed taxi driver for breaching a Public Spaces Protection Order and failing to pay a Fixed Penalty Notice, reinforcing its enforcement stance around Heathrow-adjacent residential areas. The driver was ordered to pay a £220 fine, an £88 victim surcharge and £350 in prosecution costs following a hearing at Ealing Magistrates’ Court on Monday 8 December. item.title: Regulator explores easing or potentially removing UK contactless payment limits to support growth
item.description: The UK’s Financial Conduct Authority is assessing whether removing or raising the current contactless payment limit could benefit consumers, merchants and wider economic growth, as part of a broader push to make financial regulation less prescriptive. In an engagement paper, the regulator said greater flexibility on contactless limits could deliver smoother transactions for households and businesses, while giving payment firms more control over how limits are set and managed. item.title: Manchester taxi grants raise questions over potential pressure on London’s second-hand black cab market
item.description: Greater Manchester’s £12,560 Hackney Support Fund grant is already being welcomed by drivers locally, but attention is now turning south to what the scheme could mean for London’s tightly balanced second-hand black cab market. item.title: LICENSING INQUIRY: Councils accuse Wolverhampton of fuelling cross border private hire licensing by allowing out-of-area MOT and onboarding
item.description: Salford City Council have told MPs that Wolverhampton City Council’s approach to taxi and private hire licensing has “opened up the floodgates” to drivers and vehicles operating hundreds of miles away from the city.
